summary: The note describes how interactive whiteboards have replaced chalkboards and dry-erase boards in classrooms, citing studies and educator comments on greater engagement, retention, versatility and inclusion. It also covers future AR/VR integration, cost and training challenges, and the growing emphasis on digital literacy and teacher preparation.
one_line: Interactive whiteboards are replacing traditional boards, boosting engagement, retention and inclusion, while cost, training and future AR/VR integration remain key considerations.
key_facts: Whiteboards and dry-erase markers began replacing blackboards in the early 2000s, reducing mess and health concerns from chalk dust.
Dr. Samantha Leigh, an educational technologist at the University of Clarkeston, said the tactile nature of interactive whiteboards allows a more engaging and immersive learning experience.
A study by education researcher James Aaronson, published October 10, 2023, found a 25% increase in student engagement when lessons were delivered via interactive whiteboards.

Dr. Leah Nguyen, a cognitive psychologist, said on November 16, 2023 that the multi-sensory experience anchors information in students' memories more effectively than static images or oral lectures alone.

Jake Matthews, a physical education teacher at Westside Elementary, uses interactive whiteboard activities such as 3D views of the human muscular system followed by exercise videos (reported December 5, 2023).
Maria Gonzalez, a special education teacher, helped implement a district-wide initiative in January 2024 to integrate interactive whiteboards into special education classrooms.
Interactive whiteboards let teachers alter font sizes, colors and contrast, helping students with visual impairments or dyslexia.
Michael Chen, CEO of EduTech Innovations, revealed at a conference on March 14, 2024 plans for an interactive whiteboard that syncs with AR glasses.
The cost of equipping classrooms with interactive whiteboards may be prohibitive for underfunded districts, and teacher training and maintenance add ongoing expenses.
Economist Dr. Richard Franklin projected that over time whiteboards could yield savings through reduced material costs and increased efficiency, with economies of scale lowering prices.
Teacher preparedness programs are ramping up globally to equip educators with skills for interactive technologies and digital literacy.
